study_identification_part.si4_title: Contrasting Case-Control and Normative Reference Approaches to Capture Clinically Relevant Structural Brain Abnormalities in Patients With First-Episode Psychosis Who Are Antipsychotic Naive

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To evaluate whether baseline deviations from a normative reference range in subcortical volumes are better predictors of antipsychotic treatment response than raw volumes in patients with first-episode psychosis (FEP) who were naive to antipsychotic medication.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Partial correlations (raw volumes with treatment response, adjusted for age and sex); Pearson correlations (deviations with treatment response); Z-tests to compare correlations between raw volumes and deviation measures.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: In patients with FEP, negative deviations in subcortical brain volumes (caudate, putamen, ventral diencephalon) were more strongly associated with better antipsychotic treatment response compared with raw subcortical volumes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: In a study of 98 FEP patients and 92 controls, patients with FEP showed lower raw volumes in the thalamus (P=.002), hippocampus (P=.009), amygdala (P=.01), ventral diencephalon (P=.03), and brainstem (P=.004). 36% (36 of 98) of FEP patients displayed extreme deviations, with 22% in ventricles and 22% in subcortical regions. Subcortical extreme deviations were twice as often negative. Importantly, while raw subcortical volumes did not associate with treatment response, negative deviations in the caudate, putamen, and ventral diencephalon were predictive of response. Correlations between raw volume and deviation measures significantly differed in the caudate (z=-2.17; P=.03) and putamen (z=-2.15; P=.03).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study did not exclude patients who used cannabis, which may limit generalizability. Age and sex were used as covariates for correlations with treatment response instead of total intracranial volume for consistency, though using total intracranial volume did not change results.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: This study has limitations. We did not exclude patients who used cannabis, a major risk factor for developing psychosis, as this would have limited the generalizability of our data. We included age and sex, the same variables relevant in normative modeling, rather than total intracranial volumes as covariates when computing correlations between raw volumes and treatment response. We did this to be consistent in variables considered for both models. Using total intracranial volume for raw data did not change these results (data not shown).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study demonstrated that normative modeling could capture interindividual heterogeneity and characterize structural pathology in a clinically relevant manner in FEP patients. Specifically, negative deviations in subcortical dopaminergic brain regions were more predictive of antipsychotic treatment response than raw volumes, suggesting potential for precision medicine in psychiatry.
